newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty firms vs basket in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty firms vs basket in volatile trade.

text.p: The Polish zloty finished the volatile session stronger against the basket of currencies after intraday swings initially caused by a large foreign client dollar-buying order, dealers said.

They said banks, expecting the central bank intervention this morning, joined-in on the currency-buying and later had to close positions after it became clear that the central bank had not bought currencies on the forex market today.
"After a currency-buying trend banks started to close long positions, supported by the dollar's slide against the mark," said Konrad Kolasinski of American Bank in Poland SA.
The zloty closed at 3.31/3.19 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Tuesday's 2.97/2.92 percent close.
It was at 3.0212/52 to the dollar, down from 3.0110/30 on Tuesday and at 1.7900/20 to the mark up from 1.7995/15.

Dealers said that the foreign currency-buying order which sparked today's dollar-buying trend was probably not connected with Polish T-bill transactions, but rather with a treasury redemption or a forward transaction.
"Secondary T-bill yields were unchanged despite such large disturbance on the local forex market," said Piotr Bednarek from ING Bank in Warsaw.

Currency-sale orders at the end of the session which drove the zloty to 3.12 percent from parity at the central bank's fixing came from domestic players closing sposition and partly from foreign orders, dealers said.
Many were unsure about the domestic forex outlook tomorrow with some expecting the zloty may open unchanged.

The deposit market was expected to stay underliquid on Thursday. Overnight deposit rates were quoted at 22.90/23.15 percent, up from opening's 22.80/23.00 percent, tomorrow/next were at 23.00/23.25 percent, up from 22.5/22.8 percent.
